title: Ilinca–Kahn conjectured bipartite matching entropy bound
source: Liviu Ilinca and Jeff Kahn, “Asymptotics of the Upper Matching Conjecture”, arXiv:1205.4342 (2012). (https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.4342), Conjecture 3.1, equation (20)

lanes.review: shard005-candidates-review-sol62-20261118-r1/REVIEW-323535.md (GPT-6.2 Sol, PASS; supplied the m = 3 certificate)

significance.root_decision: For every m >= 3 the bipartite graph K_{m,m+1} together with a disjoint edge, with parts of sizes m+1 and m+2, has (m+1)! matchings saturating the smaller part, which strictly exceeds the bound of Ilinca-Kahn Conjecture 3.1; the natural-log gap is about 0.0253 at m = 3 and increases. The proof uses tangents to the convex function log Gamma for m >= 4 and an exact integer chord certificate for m = 3; within this family m = 1, 2 satisfy the bound. The special case the authors were most confident of (all left degrees equal with integral t) is not refuted and remains open.
significance.caveat: The journal version of the source (JCTA 120, 2013) and journal versions of related papers are unread; the literature search was bounded.

root_basis: Root extracted the four modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, object hashes identical to the author build, axioms exactly the allowed three); read every Lean definition (IKDeg, IKNoIsolates, IKMatchings, IKCount, IKPsi2, IKConjecture, IKFamily) and the endpoints against the source statement quoted in the review; read the whole paper and rechecked equations (1) to (5) by hand, reran the exact integer comparisons, and recomputed the gap for m = 1..8 directly from the source definition (signs and values agree). Because the paper and the review are both by GPT-6.2 Sol and Opus was rate-limited, root served as the final paper referee.
